claims.text: Pregnancy test first in every patient of reproductive age, whatever the history; serum quantitative beta-hCG if the urine test is negative and pregnancy is possible.
claims.quote: All patients of reproductive age with vaginal bleeding require a urine or blood pregnancy test, regardless of menstrual or sexual history. Before 5 weeks' gestation, a urine pregnancy test may not detect the pregnancy. A quantitative serum beta human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-hCG) test should be measured if the urine test is negative and pregnancy is possible.

claims.text: Anemia: CBC for heavy, prolonged or recurring bleeding; iron studies if anemia isn't clearly iron deficiency; type and cross-match for acute heavy bleeding.
claims.quote: Anemia: For heavy, prolonged, persistent, or recurring bleeding, a complete blood count (CBC); if anemia is identified and is not obviously due to iron deficiency (eg, based on microcytic, hypochromic red blood cell [RBC] indices), iron studies (serum iron, total iron binding capacity [TIBC], and ferritin); for acute, heavy bleeding, a blood type and cross-match in case blood transfusion is needed

claims.text: Endocrine causes: TSH; total testosterone, 17-hydroxyprogesterone and DHEA-S for PCOS; prolactin; FSH if menopausal status is unclear.
claims.quote: Endocrine disorders: Depending on history and symptoms, tests for thyroid disease (thyroid-stimulating hormone), polycystic ovary syndrome (total testosterone, 17-hydroxyprogesterone,dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate), or hyperprolactinemia (prolactin); menopause is not a disorder, but if menopausal status is uncertain, test for follicle-stimulating hormone

claims.text: Bleeding disorder (heavy menses with a positive history screen): platelets, PT, aPTT and fibrinogen; von Willebrand testing if suspected.
claims.quote: Bleeding disorder: For heavy menstrual bleeding, screen the patient's history for risk factors; if screen is positive, platelet count, prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time, and fibrinogen; if von Willebrand disease is suspected, von Willebrand factor antigen, ristocetin cofactor assay, and factor VIII

claims.text: Transvaginal ultrasound for a suspected structural lesion or endometrial cancer risk factors.
claims.quote: Imaging includes transvaginal ultrasound if women have any of the following: A suspected structural lesion (based on history or examination) Risk factors for endometrial cancer

claims.text: Endometrial sampling for AUB at age > 45 years.
claims.quote: Endometrial sampling is indicated for patients with abnormal uterine bleeding combined with Age > 45 years

claims.text: Sampling is by endometrial biopsy or D & C.
claims.quote: Sampling can be performed by endometrial biopsy or dilation and curettage (D & C).

claims.text: Postmenopausal bleeding: sample when the endometrium is > 4 mm on ultrasound, or with any bleeding at high risk (eg, tamoxifen, Lynch syndrome).
claims.quote: In postmenopausal bleeding, endometrial thickening > 4 mm on ultrasound or any bleeding in patients at high risk of endometrial cancer (eg, current tamoxifen therapy, Lynch syndrome)

claims.text: Hysteroscopy is the gold standard for intrauterine structural causes; saline-infusion sonohysterography helps characterize small lesions such as polyps and submucous fibroids.
claims.quote: Secondary evaluation with saline-infusion sonohysterography helps to characterize small intrauterine lesions (eg, endometrial polyps, submucous myomas). Hysteroscopy is the gold standard for diagnosis of intrauterine structural causes of abnormal uterine bleeding.
